neet_che_u09_t03_1.working: Helium has the highest first ionization enthalpy, about 2372 kJ/mol. Its 1s² electrons are very close to the nucleus and have no shielding.

neet_che_u09_t03_2.working: Approximate first ionization enthalpies: B 801, Be 899, C 1086, O 1314, N 1402 kJ/mol. So B < Be < C < O < N.

neet_che_u09_t03_3.working: The big jump comes between the 2nd (1451) and 3rd (7733) ionization enthalpies. So X has two valence electrons; the values match Mg, a Group 2 element.

neet_che_u09_t03_4.working: A: Be > B because an s electron penetrates more than a p electron (II). B: N > O because of paired-electron repulsion in O's 2p orbital (I). C: Na's second ionization breaks a noble gas core (IV). D: ionization enthalpy falls down a group due to larger size and more shielding (III).

neet_che_u09_t03_5.working: A is true: ionization is endothermic. B is false: the second ionization enthalpy is always larger than the first. C is true: S (1000) < P (1012) kJ/mol. D is false: Al (577) < Mg (738) kJ/mol. E is true: Cs has the lowest among stable elements. So A, C and E.
